Rule: Set automatically by request size. Tier 1 is a request at or above the Tier 1 minimum in Settings: a large ask, led by the board. Tier 2 is at or above the Tier 2 minimum: a warm funder or an open call, led by the grants lead. Tier 3 is smaller: short forms and letters, drafted from your claims register.

Rate five things from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent): mission match, geography, whether they fund your kind of work, your relationship with them, and how easy their reporting is. Fit is the sum, out of 25. If Eligible is N, fit shows 0 and you stop.
Your honest guess, 0 to 100. Type 40, not 40%. A warm funder who asked you to apply might be 60. A cold application to a funder you have no tie to is often 10 or less.
Request times chance of winning, divided by the hours you expect to spend. It lets you compare a quick small ask with a long big one. It is a guide for ordering your work, not a forecast.

Use exactly: Prospect, LOI Submitted, Submitted, Pending Decision, Awarded, Awarded-Reduced, Declined, Not Pursued, Outcome Unknown, Closed. The Dashboard counts these words, so spelling matters. LOI means letter of inquiry, a short first letter some funders ask for.
Use it when nobody recorded what happened. Never guess a win or a loss.
verified means you saw it on the funder's own page or filing and wrote down the web address and date. secondary means a directory said so. unverified means you have not seen it yourself.
Before you call anyone a prospect, search your past reports, minutes and bank records for the name. A current or past funder is never a prospect.
If this sheet disagrees with a grant letter, your books or the minutes, the source document wins and this sheet gets fixed.
Type dates as mm/dd/yyyy so the sheet reads them as dates.
